== what this replay is not (the substitutions) ==
- the liquidity: ONE full-range position of the real pool's in-range liquidity at block 26049800, in a NEW pool (a hook is part
  of a pool's key: it cannot be attached to the pool that exists). The real pool's ranges, and every add and remove of
  the window, are absent: deviations grow wherever the real price crossed a tick where liquidity changed.
- the swaps: every one EXACT-IN of what the real swapper paid in, in the real direction, with no price limit, through the
  kit's MinimalRouter, by one trader. Exact-out swaps, limits, multi-hop routes, the real routers and senders are not.
- the reactions: the order is the chain's, but the swaps were placed against the REAL pool's price. A hook that changes
  what a swap pays moves this pool's price under later swaps that were never placed against it; arbitrage, MEV and
  the hook's own effect on who trades are not modelled.
- the fees: the hook pool's key has the real fee unless the hook needs another (a dynamic-fee hook sets its own, and
  its runs line shows the flag, 8388608); the protocol fee is whatever the chain's controller gives a NEW pool on the
  fork (the runs table), which need not be the real pool's (the seed line) - the swapper's output moves by the difference.
- the control: the same replay, in a test of its own, on a pool with NO hook (same currencies and fee; tick spacing
  doubled, the real key being taken), one per hook contract - control(<hook>). Its deviations are the replay's own;
  the hook's effect is the difference from ITS control (the gas of two controls can differ by a few units: the test
  contracts' own code differs).
